stages.6: Phase 6 — No-code Hardware Studio and automation

items.feature: Audit of existing HANNAH and what is reused
items.note: A section of the architecture page. Reused: Action Engine, permission manager, vault, webhooks, workflows, model gateway, agents, document reader, the robot runtime's protocol design.

items.feature: Three parts kept apart: edge hub, control plane, clients
items.note: Three separate processes in the tests. A client never talks to a device; the server never connects to a hub.

items.feature: Hardware compatibility strategy: levels computed from evidence
items.note: plug-and-play, guided, experimental, simulation, developer required, unsupported. Nothing that ships is plug-and-play.

items.feature: No real-time control and no raw addressing above an adapter
items.note: An adapter exposes named points only. Deterministic control stays in the device, an MCU or the robot's controller.

items.feature: Evaluation of the Linux foundation: Ubuntu Server, Ubuntu Core, Yocto/OpenEmbedded
items.note: A written evaluation with the choice per image profile. Not validated by a build.

items.feature: Five image profiles that share one core, and a manifest that is the same every time
items.note: This verifies the description and the manifest. It is not an image.

items.feature: Building the images (ubuntu-image, snapcraft, Yocto)
items.note: Build inputs are written and have never been built.

items.feature: Installation, boot and first-boot setup on a board
items.note: The first-boot configuration is written and has never been booted.

items.feature: The hub as a hardened system service
items.note: Written on a machine without systemd; never started.

items.feature: Hub identity: one-time enrollment code, key sealed in the vault, fingerprint on both sides
Hub health check (doctor)
Secure boot, signed images, disk encryption
items.note: They belong to the image build (2.3). Ubuntu Core offers them on supported hardware; nothing was configured.

items.feature: Separate, fault-isolated system services (discovery, adapters, automation, telemetry, updates)
items.note: Today the hub is one process with one thread per device connection and per command. One device's fault doesn't stop the others (tested), but they are not separate services.

items.feature: Device registry: owner, hub, maker, model, category, protocol, points, permissions, connection, health, last seen
items.note: Not in the model: workspaces (a device belongs to one account), and a device's firmware version (no protocol here reports it).

items.feature: Device Profile Package: declarative, versioned, validated
Profile signatures: Ed25519, trusted keys, revocation, a review of what it can change
items.note: The check exists. There is no screen to add a publisher's key or install a published profile yet (13.2).

items.feature: Protocol adapter framework: each adapter declares protocol, sign-in, limits, errors, security and how far it was tested
MQTT 3.1.1 adapter (QoS 0 and 1, TLS, user name and password)
items.note: Tested against HANNAH's own test broker and against aedes, an independent broker. Not against Mosquitto or any device. No QoS 2, no MQTT 5.

items.feature: Modbus TCP adapter (function codes 1-6 and 16; 16/32-bit and float formats)
items.note: Tested against HANNAH's own test server only. Local network addresses only.

items.feature: HTTP adapter for local devices
items.note: Tested against a local test server. Not part of the end-to-end tests.

items.feature: Device Safety Gateway on the server, repeated on the hub
One inventory across robots and devices
items.note: A single /api/inventory answer combines robots, devices and hubs. No dedicated screen yet.

items.feature: Guided onboarding: pick, connect, check, switch on
Verification report: connection, sign-in, encryption, data heard per point, values that fit; identity marked not checked
Looking at an MQTT broker's topics, with the person's say-so
items.note: The hub side and the server route are tested, and the Devices and Hardware Studio screens have a button for it.

items.feature: Listing serial ports
items.note: Lists paths only; opens nothing. No test.

items.feature: QR codes
items.note: Client-side QR scan via BarcodeDetector with a manual-entry fallback. No server-side QR handling yet.

items.feature: mDNS and local-network discovery
items.note: Hub can browse one mDNS service type on demand (best-effort parser). Client button not wired yet.

items.feature: USB device discovery
Bluetooth Low Energy scanning
Matter commissioning
Unknown devices: say what is missing, keep the proposal, never enable it
items.note: The answer names the missing protocol or driver. It is not stored as a request anyone is notified of.

items.feature: Reading a manual (PDF, Word, text) with page numbers
items.note: Text only. A scanned PDF has no text layer and is reported as unreadable.

items.feature: Facts with value, page, the line quoted, confidence and a verification state
items.note: Pattern-based: identity, protocol, serial settings, unit number, port, address, topics, register rows, operating limits, safety lines.

items.feature: Evidence gate: a suggested value is dropped unless its quote is on the cited page and contains the value
items.note: Applies to this code's own patterns and to anything a model suggests.

items.feature: A language or vision model reading the manual
items.note: analyze() accepts an optional suggester; accept() gates every suggestion. No model is wired by default (H5).

items.feature: Proposed profile from a manual, usable only after the hub connects with it
items.note: Always experimental. A writable register is proposed read-only; a register with no stated table is left out.

items.feature: Diagrams, wiring diagrams, product labels, images
Electrical values reported for a qualified person, never used
A manual is data: it cannot allow a write or grant a permission
Hardware Studio: describe a device with a form; the server says what is missing
Mapping sensors and actuators: type, unit, range, topic or register
Visual automation builder
items.note: One condition and one change, with the opposite when it stops. The server accepts up to four of each.

items.feature: Automation from plain language, through an agent tool
items.note: The tool and its routing are tested with a scripted server. No live model has used it (H5).

items.feature: Deterministic rules on the hub: hysteresis, hold time, stale readings, hourly limit, pause
items.note: No model is involved. Runs with the server away.

items.feature: Developer mode: the generated description is shown
items.note: Shown in the Studio; no test asserts it.

items.feature: Trying a change from the Studio before switching a device on
Schedules, variables, retries and error branches for device actions
items.note: The existing workflow engine can call device actions and is triggered by device.alert and device.rule.fired; combination still has no end-to-end test.

items.feature: Robot runtime, simulators, Safety Gateway, missions, plans
items.note: Tracked in robotics/PROGRESS.md, with its own tests (server/robotics.*.test.js).

items.feature: ROS 2, Gazebo, Nav2
items.note: Written, never run. See robotics/PROGRESS.md.

items.feature: Physical robots and physical devices
items.note: Nothing has been connected.

items.feature: IoT runtime: readings in, state kept with its age, events, reconnection, working offline
Matter
Zigbee, Z-Wave, Bluetooth Low Energy
OPC UA
items.note: Needs a client library with certificate handling and a server to test against.

items.feature: Modbus RTU, CAN, raw serial, GPIO/I2C/SPI, CoAP
items.note: Each is listed in the app as not built, with what it needs. CAN is out of scope by design.

items.feature: Profiles for real products
items.note: None ships. Writing one without the device to test it would be a guess.

items.feature: Device events for webhooks and workflows
items.note: Device events are offered to webhooks and workflow triggers (device.alert, device.rule.fired).

items.feature: Devices agent, ten tools, routing by what the person says
Voice: a spoken request reaches the same tools
items.note: A transcript takes the same road as typed text (tested on sentences). Speech recognition with device requests was not tested.

items.feature: Device and configuration history in memory
items.note: A device's events and changes are kept in the registry, not in HANNAH's memory.

items.feature: Model gateway
items.note: Existing: 20 providers including OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, xAI, DeepSeek, Mistral, Groq, Cerebras, OpenRouter, Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM and custom endpoints (server/gateway.test.js). Not built: Azure AI and Amazon Bedrock. MLX works through a custom endpoint.

items.feature: Manipulation
items.note: Arm simulator verified; MoveIt 2 not started. Tracked in robotics/PROGRESS.md.

items.feature: Robot fleet
items.note: Tracked in robotics/PROGRESS.md.

items.feature: Several hubs in one account
items.note: The registry and the screen handle several; the tests use one.

items.feature: Signed profile packages with a review before use
Marketplace: publish, browse, install, revoke, roll back
items.note: Account-level publisher keys and a verified install of a signed profile (verifyProfile + saveProfile).

items.feature: SDKs for devices (profile, adapter, workflow)
items.note: The profile format and the HTTP API are documented. A robot client exists (robotics/sdk/js); none for devices.

items.feature: Third-party driver code on a hub
items.note: By design nothing third-party runs on a hub today: a profile is data. Running a contributed adapter needs a sandbox and a review step.

items.feature: Hub self-update: announced hash, safe unpack, health check, probation, rollback
items.note: The module only. It is not wired to a server command and has never replaced an installed hub.

items.feature: Update distribution: signed command, staged rollout, fleet view
items.note: Hub handles an update command (stage, activate, rollback on restart); server can announce one and report status; client can announce.

items.feature: Operating-system image updates and rollback
items.note: Planned through Ubuntu Core's own transactional updates for the gateway profiles.

items.feature: The hub keeps its signed configuration and resumes from it
items.note: A configuration edited on disk is not obeyed.

items.feature: Device firmware updates
items.note: Not planned as an AI action. A profile cannot expose firmware, reset or pairing as a point (tested).

items.feature: Security tests: forged and replayed hub requests, wrong hub, expired and replayed commands, edited configuration, malicious profile, wildcard topics, untrusted manual text, cross-account access, out-of-range and unallowed writes, unsafe update archives
Existing HANNAH still works: whole server, client and browser suites
items.note: See the last full verification below.

items.feature: No-code acceptance: add a hub, add a device, check, switch on, change, automate, see history
items.note: With simulated devices and a hub started by hand. Step 1 of the acceptance list, installing the operating environment on a target, is not done (2.3, 2.4).

items.feature: Independent security review
Performance measurements
items.note: None taken. No figure is claimed anywhere.

items.feature: Landing page and README say what works and what doesn't

blockers.what: No physical device, broker, PLC or machine to test against
blockers.needs: The owner names a device (maker, model) and has it on a network with a hub
blockers.unblocks: Real product profiles, plug-and-play, any claim about a physical device

blockers.what: No Linux build host with ubuntu-image or snapcraft, and no board to boot
blockers.needs: A Linux machine (or CI job) and a target board or virtual machine
blockers.unblocks: Building, booting and updating HANNAH OS images

blockers.what: No Matter controller, Zigbee or Z-Wave coordinator, or Bluetooth radio, and no stack for them on the hub
blockers.needs: The radio hardware, a decision on the library for each, and a device to pair

blockers.what: No ROS 2, Gazebo or robot (robotics blockers B1 to B3)
blockers.unblocks: Everything robotics that says Gazebo, ROS 2 or hardware

blockers.what: No live language model run in the development environment
blockers.needs: A provider key the owner is willing to use for tests
blockers.unblocks: Model-assisted manual reading; showing an agent using device tools with a real model

blockers.needs: A reviewer who did not write the code
blockers.unblocks: Any statement that the security design was reviewed

next: Wire the hub's self-update to a signed server command, with a staged rollout and a fleet view (14.2).
A button for looking at a broker's topics, and a server test for it (4.3); offer the topics found in the Hardware Studio.
A test for device events reaching a webhook and starting a workflow (9.7, 6.8).
Call a model for manual reading behind the evidence gate, off by default, with the provider named before anything is sent (5.4).
One inventory across robots and devices (3.9).
QR codes and mDNS, each as a named, person-authorised look (4.5, 4.6).
A publisher-key screen and installing a signed profile (13.2).

cd hannah-os/runtime && python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .
cd client && npx vitest run src/__tests__/Devices.test.ts && npm run build && npx playwright test hardware.spec.ts
python3 -m hannah_edge simulate    # from hannah-os/runtime: simulated devices to try the Devices screen with
